I make mistakes and take losses in my weekly trading just like with swingtrading. We learn for every day we are in the market. 

But I wanted to show you what the benefit can be when trading on weekly charts. If you havent read my educational post on it, you should, because trading on the weekly is a different animal that needs a different approach. 

It is much more forgiving and it matters much more if you have assessed the theme and the structure correctly. 

My focus in cyber was $RBRK because it has the base, the weekly structure, the growth and also that it's a young IPO. And I bought the second week it pulled back into the 10 weekly SMA after a strong run, a classic O'Neil entry tactic. And I almost top ticked that week, but zooming out the setup is valid, it just tested the weekly 10 SMA again so there is no reason to sell it. 

Stocks will all the time violate and shakeout under the weekly 10 SMA only to reclaim it and explode higher after, what makes it likely or not that they will recover is the structure and strength that precedes that spot.

中国访美：要看的几条线
中国这次访美，市场已经开始提前交易三个东西：企业代表团、具体 Deal和科技限制会不会边际放松。

目前 Reuters 明确点名、属于高概率候选的企业包括比亚迪 BYD、宁德时代 CATL、小米 Xiaomi、国轩高科 Gotion、海信 Hisense、万向集团、中国银行以及中粮集团 COFCO。不过要注意，目前企业代表团还没有最终敲定，所以这些属于媒体确认正在考虑，不是官方最终名单。另外中际旭创 Innolight 也被媒体单独点名。如果最终确定随行，我会比较关注，因为它对应的是AI 数据中心和光通信产业链。

如果后面再出现 Alibaba、Baidu、Tencent 这种大型互联网和 AI 企业，那市场交易逻辑就会进一步看AI、Cloud、芯片出口限制有没有谈判空间。这一部分目前还是我的预测，后面几天继续等名单。

从已经曝光的企业来看，美股有很清晰的产业链映射。

中际旭创（AI 光通信）：COHR / LITE / AAOI / MRVL，另外上游 InP 材料可以观察 AXTI。

CATL / BYD / 国轩高科（电池、EV、储能）：F / GM / ALB / TSLA。 其中 Ford 与 CATL 本身就存在电池技术授权合作，所以 F 的关联更加直接。

小米 / 海信（消费电子、智能终端）：QCOM / ARM，主要交易中国消费电子需求以及美国芯片供应商对中国市场的敞口。

万向集团（汽车零部件、新能源供应链）：F / GM 以及美国汽车产业链。

中粮集团 COFCO（农业贸易）： ADM / BG。 如果这次最终落地美国大豆、玉米等农产品采购，中粮可能是值得重点观察的执行端之一。Reuters 也确认农业采购是此次会谈的重要议题。

如果后续代表团再出现 Alibaba / Baidu 等 AI 企业，那会进一步扩大到 NVDA / AMD / AVGO / MRVL，因为市场会开始交易 AI 芯片出口限制是否存在边际放松的可能。现在北京也确实在推动美国进一步延后部分科技限制，而美国希望中国增加稀土和关键矿产出口。

这次具体采购 Deal 可能是最直接的催化。目前已经值得观察的包括：飞机（BA），农业 （ADM / BG），能源 （LNG / XOM / CVX），稀土限制放松（美国汽车、半导体、航空航天等下游制造业）。

还有一条要关注的是 Apple / CXMT。 如果这次谈判推动美国允许 Apple 在中国市场采购 CXMT（长鑫存储）的 DRAM，对 AAPL 属于供应链多元化和成本端潜在利好，但对 MU 会形成一定竞争压力。如果未来进一步涉及 YMTC 的 NAND，那对 SNDK 的影响会更直接。现在这条还属于潜在 Deal，不是已经确定的谈判结果。

Boeing，Reuters 报道双方之前已经谈到 200 架飞机，而且潜在协议可能进一步扩大到 500 架 737 MAX和数十架宽体机。如果 9 月 24 日真的出现大订单，BA 会是非常直接的 Deal 映射。

这几天就看谁最终谁进入企业代表团、双方交换了什么条件、最后有没有落地的大额采购和科技限制调整。

One thing I keep reminding myself as a pullback trader:

If you really liked a stock yesterday, and today or tomorrow it gives you a clean backtest into your key moving averages, you probably shouldn’t suddenly hate it just because it printed 1–3 red days.

Assuming the thesis and structure are still intact, you should often like it more, not less.

Same stock. Same setup. Lower price.

Your R:R just improved — but psychologically, this is usually the exact moment people remove it from the watchlist.

That’s the funny part about buying weakness: the opportunity often looks less comfortable right when it gets better.

We’re almost 9 months into 2026, with just 3 months left. 

I was going through my journal this morning and realized I’ve only made around 35 closed entries this entire year, outside of my current 13 holdings. A few years ago, that number could’ve easily been 200+.

Yet with far less activity, I’m sitting close to +90% YTD.

The biggest change has been learning to think longer term with more patience and discipline - find the right themes early, own the strongest businesses, get the technicals + fundamentals right, build a good cost basis, size appropriately, and then give the thesis enough time to play out.

I can’t emphasize enough how big of a role discipline has played in my journey. Finding a great stock is one thing. Having the discipline to sit tight and let it work is another.

Semiconductors were easily my biggest win this year.

I realized significant gains across several semiconductor names while continuing to hold a few leaders in the theme.

And another major lesson: position sizing matters.

Many of my winners started around 5% and naturally grew into 10-15%+ positions as the stocks appreciated. Most of my losing positions were around 2-3%, or generally less than 5% of the portfolio, so when I was wrong, the impact on the overall portfolio remained relatively small.

During the June/July pullback, I started positioning into software, crypto, newer semiconductor names and a few other themes that I believe have long-term potential.

The more I refine my framework, the more I realize: Less is more. I’ve evolved into a position trader and long-term investor. I’d rather own the right leaders, sit through normal volatility, let the fundamentals compound and give the bigger trend time to play out.

You don’t build outsized returns by making more decisions. You build them by making the right decisions and having the patience to sit tight.

One of the most important skills you must develop as you grow as an investor or trader is pattern recognition.

And I’m not just talking about recognizing a cup & handle, bull flag or double bottom.

Technical analysis is really the study of human psychology expressed through price and volume. Fear, greed, FOMO, capitulation, accumulation and distribution - all eventually show up on the chart.

Different stocks. Different years. Different narratives. But human behavior doesn’t change much.

A breakout on strong volume tells you buyers are becoming more aggressive. A tight consolidation after a massive move tells you there isn’t much selling pressure. Heavy distribution tells you institutions may be heading for the exits. A long Stage 1 base can show you that months of selling pressure are slowly being absorbed.

This is why I spend so much time studying historical charts. The more charts you study, the more you start seeing the same behaviors repeat themselves across different stocks and different market cycles.

Eventually, you stop looking at a chart and simply seeing lines and patterns. You start understanding the battle between buyers and sellers behind them.

You’re not just memorizing patterns. You’re training your brain to recognize human behavior repeating itself in the market.

That’s what technical analysis is really about.
